description.cancellation_policy:
Cancellation Policy: Please cancel your reservation if you are unable to use it! This ensures the space will be available for others. You may cancel up to the day of your reservation date. All fees are non-refundable; however, if you do not cancel your reservation, you will not be able to make another reservation in the same month.

In the event that the Forest Service is required to close the Fossil Creek Permit Area due to weather, natural disasters or fire danger, all reservations in this instance only will receive a full refund.

Change Policy: Changing the date of your reservation requires you to cancel your existing reservation and make a new reservation, should space be available. The $6.00 reservation fee is non-refundable.
description.description:
The Bob Bear Trailhead is accessed via Fossil Creek Rd from the town of Strawberry.

The Bob Bear Trail provides access to the headwaters of the Fossil Creek Wild and Scenic River and the Fossil Springs Wilderness on the Tonto and Coconino National Forests. The trail begins at an elevation of 5,700 feet on Deadman Mesa near the town of Strawberry and descends 1,500 feet over 4 miles into the Fossil Creek canyon. The trail offers a remote, backcountry experience and is steep and extremely hot during the summer, but rewards visitors with access to one of Arizona’s most spectacular riparian areas.

No water and little shade are available for the first 3.75 miles of the trail. Summer temperatures regularly exceed 100 degrees F. Cell phone coverage is unreliable. Visitors must come prepared for being out a full day, with plenty of food and water (at least a gallon per person is recommended), sturdy footwear (no flip flops!), and good physical fitness. Every year unprepared visitors require rescue from this trail, risking the lives of themselves and emergency responders. 

Advance permits are required to park a vehicle in the Fossil Creek permit area April 1–October 1. During this season, a maximum of one permit per person per month may be reserved. Maximum group size 12. Minimum age of permit holder is 18.

The Fossil Creek area has very few developed facilities and visitors should be prepared for rustic and remote conditions. There is no camping in the Fossil Creek Permit Area from April 1 through October 1.

Fossil Creek will only be open Friday- Sunday for Month of April the 2026 permit season (April 1st-April 31st). Fossil Creek will be closed Monday - Thursday and vehicles will be prohibited from parking along the roadway within the permit area or at Bob Bear Trailhead on the Tonto National Forest.

Permits are not required October 2–March 31.
description.driving_directions:
• From Payson: 18 mi north on Hwy 87 to Strawberry. OR
  • From Camp Verde/I-17: Exit 287, 34 mi east on Hwy 260 toward Payson to intersection with Hwy 87. Right on Hwy 87 and drive 8 mi; THEN
  • West on Fossil Creek Road for 5 miles then a right turn to the Bob Bear Trailhead

description.need_to_know_email:
The Bob Bear Trail hike is long (8 miles round-trip), steep (1,500 feet down and 1,500 feet back up), and hot (summer temps often exceed 100 degrees F) with very little shade and no water, making it one of the most difficult trails on the Tonto National Forest.  

You must print your permit. Cell phone screen shots will not be accepted as a permit. The permit holder must carry the permit and the parking pass must be displayed on your vehicle's dashboard. You may print your permit when you make your reservation; however, once you print your permit, you can not make changes to the permit.

The confirmation email is not your permit. If you do not print your permit when you make the reservation you must log into your Recreation.Gov account and access your reservations to print your permit. When you print your permit 3 pages will print at the same time. The permit page, rules/regulations page and the parking pass required for entry. 

Please cancel your reservation if you are unable to use it. This ensures the space will be available for others. You may cancel up to the day of your reservation date. All fee are non-refundable; however, if you do not cancel your reservation, you will not be able to make another reservation in the same month.

If you need to change the date of your reservation, you will need to cancel your existing reservation and make a new one, should space be available. The $6.00 reservation fee is non-refundable.  

Access to the Bob Bear Trail may be closed due to weather events or natural disasters to protect public safety. For more information, visit the Tonto NF website at www.fs.usda.gov/tonto. If a closure occurs, all reservations will receive a full refund. 

Every year unprepared people are rescued along this remote trail, making emergency personnel unavailable to serve their local communities. Plan ahead and be prepared.
description.need_to_know_order:
Below you will find important information regarding your trip on the Bob Bear Trail. Please carefully review the information and click the check box to acknowledge you have done so. 

  • Please cancel your reservation if you are unable to use it to ensure the space will be available for others. 

  • Access to the area may be closed to protect public safety. For more information, visit the Tonto NF website https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/

  • You must print your permit and parking pass. 

  • This trail does not access the waterfall!

  • Be prepared for a remote setting with few amenities and extreme summer heat. Do not attempt to hike the Bob Bear Trail without adequate water, food, footwear, and physical fitness. The Bob Bear Trailhead does not provide direct access to the creek.

  • Do not rely on your GPS or mapping software to get to the trailhead; their directions may be incorrect. Please review the directions provided in the Getting Here section on Recreation.gov. A section of Forest Road 708 between Strawberry and the Fossil Creek canyon is closed and there is no access to the waterfall or parking lots in the Fossil Creek canyon via FR 708 from Strawberry.

  • No trash service is available and toilets are limited. Please pack out what you bring. A toilet is available at the parking lot. 

  • Cell phone reception in the area is virtually nonexistent. 

  • No potable water is available; you must bring your own water.

  • No campfires, warming fires or charcoal grills are allowed anywhere within the permit area, ever. If you plan to cook, bring your own gas stove.

  • There is no camping in the Fossil Creek permit area April 1–October 1.

  • Vehicles exceeding 22 feet in length are prohibited, including buses and vans. Vehicles with trailers are prohibited except for equestrians. All persons must be accommodated inside the vehicle with a legal seatbelt.

  • Glass containers are prohibited in the permit area.
description.need_to_know_permit:
The Bob Bear Trail hike is long (8 miles round-trip), steep (1,500 feet down and 1,500 feet back up), and hot (summer temps often exceed 100 degrees F) with very little shade and no water, making it one of the most difficult trails on the Tonto National Forest.  

  • This trail does not access the waterfall and does not provide direct access to the creek. 

  • Do not rely on your GPS or mapping software to get to the trailhead; the directions may be incorrect.  

  • Please do not attempt to hike this trail without adequate water, food, footwear, and physical fitness.  

  • You must bring your own water.  

  • Every year unprepared people are rescued along this remote trail, making emergency personnel unavailable to serve their local communities. 

  • Plan ahead and be prepared.  

  • You must print your permit and parking pass. The permit holder must carry the permit and the parking pass must be placed on your vehicle’s dashboard.  

  • There is no camping in the Fossil Creek permit area April 1–October 1.  

  • A toilet is provided in the parking area only.  

  • No rope swings may be installed along the river.  

  • Glass containers are prohibited in the permit area.  

  • No amplified sound (music or loudspeakers) is allowed in Forest Service facilities.  

  • There is very limited cell service in this area. 

  • Tampering with or removing cultural and historic sites and artifacts is illegal.  

  • No campfires, or charcoal grills are allowed anywhere within the permit area.  

  • If you plan to cook, bring your own gas stove.  

  • Use reasonable caution and check the weather forecast: the trail is rugged and steep; flash flooding may occur; be aware of fire danger.
description.no_show_policy: No Show Policy: If you do not cancel your reservation, you will not be able to make another reservation in the same month.
description.quota_details:
The quota for this permit is measured by vehicle. One permit equals one parking spot for one vehicle for one day.

On March 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of April, Friday - Sunday only.

On April 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of May.

On May 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of June.

On June 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of July.

On July 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of August.

On August 1, permits are available to purchase for the following month of September and October 1.
description.season_information:
Advance permits are required to park a vehicle in the Fossil Creek permit area April 1–October 1. During this season, a maximum of one permit per person per calendar month may be reserved (one permit=one day). Permits are made available on the first of the month one month ahead of time. For example, permits for the month of April are available beginning March 1.

The permit allows parking for one vehicle only at the Bob Bear Trailhead parking lot. Maximum vehicle length is 22 ft. All persons listed on the permit must be accommodated inside the vehicle with a legal seatbelt. The permit guarantees parking within the specified parking lot, but specific parking space assignments are not made. Parking spaces are occupied on a first-come, first-serve basis.

Permits are not required October 2–March 31.

Equestrian users may reserve an assigned parking space for a vehicle and horse trailer. The maximum vehicle and horse trailer length combined is 50 ft.

See 'Need to Know' section for more info.

425190301.description: The Bob Bear Trailhead is the start of the 4-mile Bob Bear Trail, which accesses the headwaters of Fossil Creek and the Fossil Springs Wilderness. The parking lot does not provide direct access to Fossil Creek! This hike is long (8 miles round-trip), steep (1,500 feet down and 1,500 feet back up), and hot (summer temps often exceed 100 degrees F) with little shade and no water, making it one of the most difficult trails on the Tonto National Forest. Please do not attempt to hike this trail without adequate water, food, footwear, and physical fitness. The parking lot is accessible via Forest Road 708 from Strawberry. FR 708 is closed beyond the parking lot entrance and does not access the waterfall or parking areas in the Fossil Creek canyon.

description_map.need_to_know: The parking lot does not provide direct access to the creek! Restrooms and a kiosk are available at the parking area. The parking lot is a dirt surface; no potable water or trash service. The maximum vehicle length in this parking lot is 22 feet except for horse trailers. This parking lot can accommodate horse trailers (three parking spaces available; max vehicle/trailer length of 50 feet) and has a horse hitching rail. Your reservation may be validated on-site. Parking lot is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. The access gate to this lot is open from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The access gate will close at 4 p.m. daily; however, you may still exit the parking lot after 4 p.m.
